reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about heat-treatment-induced nanotwins, dislocation density, oxide scale formation, and their effects on wear in FeNiCrCoCu coatings, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) only addresses general lattice distortion effects on structural and mechanical properties in simplified models, with no mention of the alloy, coating form, heat treatment, or wear behavior. Thus, the key premises are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Moderate heat treatment (~500 °C) of as-sprayed FeNiCrCoCu induces nanotwins and high dislocation density
The same treatment forms a thin, adherent protective oxide scale rich in Cr and Cu
These microstructural changes increase microhardness and reduce high-temperature wear
Higher temperature treatments cause grain coarsening, reducing hardness and worsening wear
The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the role of lattice distortion in structural/mechanical properties of HEAs
